rationale: The composite, spike-in–controlled mucin+device compatibility test is scientifically plausible and appropriate as an early CMC gate but carries high, actionable uncertainty (assay-interference risks, need to validate spike-in representativeness and protease access, lot-to-lot reproducibility, and lack of evidence linking an in vitro pass to large-animal/human intranasal delivery). Proceeding requires human choices and prequalification steps (approve spike-in and capture panels, define buffer/compatibility controls and qualitative acceptance rules, select device/excipient matrix and lot strategy) before committing resources to experimental execution or scale-up.
